source_text: Quae divisio naturali peccato non potest convenire, quod si esset, omnes prorsus aequaliter colligaret; nemo ergo esset, cui malum hoc non inesset, et nullus inveniretur, de quo vere posset dici, quia in similitudine peccati illius non deliquisset, in cuius omnes veritate peccassent.
pass_a_gloss: Which division cannot fit a natural sin, which if it were, would bind all altogether equally; no one therefore would be in whom this evil was not, and no one would be found of whom it could truly be said that he had not offended in a likeness of that sin, in whose truth all had sinned.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: This division cannot fit natural sin, which, if it existed, would bind absolutely everyone equally. No one, then, would lack this evil, and no one could truthfully be described as not having sinned in the likeness of that sin in whose reality everyone had sinned.

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
